verifications.claim: Meissen is a Saxon town near Dresden.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: situated about 25 km (16 mi) north‑west of Dresden ... in the Free State of Saxony
verifications.reasoning: Directly states location in Saxony near Dresden.

verifications.claim: As of 2023, the population of Meissen is approximately 29,051.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.reasoning: Reference provides a specific different population figure (28,753) for 2024, contradicting the claimed 2023 figure of approximately 29,051.

verifications.claim: The Meissen Porcelain Manufactory was established in 1710 by Augustus the Strong.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'since 1710'; R3: 'in 1710 the Meissen factory was established ... Augustus the Strong'; R4: 'manufactured in Meissen in 1710 ... Augustus II the Strong'; R5: 'founded in 1710 by Augustus the Strong'; R6: 'started in 1710 ... Augustus the Strong'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm establishment in 1710 by Augustus the Strong.

verifications.claim: The Meissen Porcelain Manufactory was the first European factory to produce true hard-paste porcelain.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the first monarch in Europe to produce his own ‘true’ porcelain'; R4: 'first high‑quality porcelain to be produced outside the Orient'; R6: 'the first European hard-paste porcelain'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Meissen as the first in Europe for true/hard-paste porcelain.

verifications.claim: The Crossed Swords mark was established in 1720 to protect its unique porcelain designs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Its signature logo, the crossed swords, was introduced in 1720 to protect its production
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on year and purpose of the mark.

verifications.claim: Meissen has over 1,000 years of history.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'looks back on more than 1,000 years of history'; R4: 'porcelain carillon ... to mark the town’s millennial jubilee' (1929, referencing ~929 origins)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R2; R4 supports with millennial reference.

verifications.claim: Albrechtsburg Castle was the former seat of the Wettin dynasty.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Albrechtsburg, former residence of the House of Wettin
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as former residence of the Wettin dynasty.

verifications.claim: Albrechtsburg Castle is Germany's first castle built as a residence rather than a fortress.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Germany's first castle to be built solely as a residence'; R4: 'first castle to be used as a royal residence in the German‑speaking world'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly matches phrasing; R4 closely supports.

verifications.claim: Meissen Cathedral is a Gothic landmark adjacent to Albrechtsburg Castle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Construction of Meissen Cathedral commenced in 1260 on the same hill as the Albrechtsburg castle'; R2: 'Meissen's Gothic cathedral'
verifications.reasoning: Gothic confirmed; same hill indicates adjacency.

verifications.claim: The Church of Our Lady houses a unique porcelain carillon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'porcelain carillon in the tower of the Gothic Church of Our Lady'; R4: 'tower houses the world’s first porcelain carillon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly confirmed as housing the porcelain carillon, described as world's first (unique).

verifications.claim: Meissen is situated on the Saxon Wine Route along the Elbe River.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'All along the Saxon Wine Route ... perched high above the Elbe River'; R4: 'on both banks of the River Elbe ... Saxonian wine region — one of the northernmost in Europe'
verifications.reasoning: Confirms location on Elbe and association with Saxon Wine Route/region.

verifications.claim: Meissen was founded as a margraviate by Henry the Fowler in the 10th century.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: In 929, King Henry the Fowler ... founded the fortress of Misnia ... Emperor Otto I founded the Margraviate ... with Meissen as its capital
verifications.reasoning: 929 (10th century) by Henry the Fowler; developed into margraviate with Meissen as capital.

verifications.claim: Augustus the Strong founded the porcelain factory in Meissen in 1710, breaking the Asian monopoly on porcelain production.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'in 1710 the Meissen factory was established ... remained a mystery to Europeans'; R4: 'first high‑quality porcelain to be produced outside the Orient'; R6: 'first European hard-paste porcelain'
verifications.reasoning: Founding confirmed; first European production directly implies breaking Asian monopoly.
